blocks.content: The salaries and conditions of service of constitutional post-holders are protected to ensure independent and impartial functioning.

items: Expenditure 'charged upon' the Consolidated Fund of India can be discussed by Parliament but is NOT subject to voting.
Differentiate retirement ages carefully: UPSC/CAG/SC Judges retire at 65, while SPSC members and High Court Judges retire at 62.
Financial Emergency (Article 360) is the only instance where salaries of constitutional office-bearers can be reduced.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tenure for major constitutional heads like the CAG and UPSC members is 6 years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Salaries and allowances of constitutional dignitaries are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India to ensure financial independence.
Conditions of service and salary cannot be varied to their disadvantage after their appointment, except during a Financial Emergency.
Upon retirement, key constitutional post-holders like the CAG and UPSC Chairman are ineligible for further employment under the Government of India or any State.
